# Skill Reviewer

Audits one or more Claude Code skills against the structural and quality
standards from Anthropic's official `skill-development` reference
(`plugin-dev` plugin), adapted for personal single-file skills as well as
plugin skills with `references/`, `examples/`, `scripts/`.

## Process

1. **Locate the target skill(s).** If the user names a skill, find its
   directory (check `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`, `~/dotfiles/claude/skills/<name>/`,
   or a project-local `.claude/skills/<name>/`). If the user says "review my
   skills" with no name, enumerate all `SKILL.md` files under the relevant
   skills directory.
2. **Read `SKILL.md` in full**, plus the full contents of any `references/`,
   `examples/`, `scripts/` subdirectories it points to.
3. **Run the checklist below** against each skill.
4. **Report findings** as a flat list, grouped by skill if reviewing more
   than one. For each finding: what's wrong, why it matters, and a concrete
   fix — not just "this could be better." Do not pad the report with checklist
   items that passed; only report what looks off, then close with a short
   verdict ("well-formed", "needs the fixes above", etc.). If applying fixes,
   confirm with the user before editing anything.

## Checklist

### Frontmatter

- `name` and `description` are present. `name` is kebab-case and matches the
  directory name exactly.
- `description` is **third-person** ("This skill should be used when...") —
  never "Use this skill when..." or "Load this when you...".
- `description` names **concrete trigger phrases** a user would actually
  type, in quotes, not vague category words. Compare:
  - Bad: `Provides guidance for working with hooks.`
  - Good: `This skill should be used when the user asks to "create a hook", "add a PreToolUse hook", "validate tool use"...`
- `description` also covers *when the skill does NOT apply*, if the trigger
  is easily confused with a nearby skill (e.g. `code-review` vs
  `security-review` vs this skill's own turf).
- No first-person or second-person voice anywhere in frontmatter.

### Body writing style

- Written in **imperative/infinitive form** ("Validate the input", "Run the
  script"), not second person ("You should validate...", "You need to run...").
  This is a real, checkable defect — grep the body for `you should`, `you need`,
  `you can`, `you must` as a fast signal.
- No unexplained jargon or unstated assumptions about prior context — a skill
  loads into a **fresh** Claude instance with none of this conversation's
  context, unlike this session's own communication norms.
- No filler restating what's already obvious from headings/names.

### Structure & progressive disclosure

- `SKILL.md` body is lean — flag if it's pushing past ~2,000 words for a
  single-file skill, or past ~3,000 words when it also has `references/`.
  Long detailed material (schemas, exhaustive examples, migration guides)
  belongs in `references/*.md`, loaded only when needed, not inlined.
- Every file the body references (`references/x.md`, `scripts/y.sh`,
  `examples/z.json`) actually exists — check with `ls`/`find`, don't assume.
- Conversely, no orphaned files in `references/`, `scripts/`, `examples/`
  that the body never points to — dead weight that never gets loaded.
- Scripts in `scripts/` are executable (`ls -l`, check the `x` bit) and, if
  feasible, actually run without error.
- No secrets, tokens, or credentials embedded in any file.

### Scope & overlap

- The skill's trigger conditions don't meaningfully overlap with another
  installed skill's triggers in a way that would make Claude's choice
  ambiguous (e.g. two skills both claiming "review code"). List the other
  skill and the overlapping phrase if found.
- The skill isn't so narrowly scoped that it's really just an instruction
  that belongs in a `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` instead of a discoverable skill,
  nor so broadly scoped ("use when doing anything with Python") that it will
  false-trigger constantly.

### Sanity checks specific to this user's setup

- If the skill lives under `~/dotfiles/claude/skills/`, confirm it's a real
  file in the repo (not accidentally created only under `~/.claude/skills/`,
  which is a symlink into dotfiles — a file placed on the wrong side of that
  symlink won't get picked up, or won't survive a fresh machine bootstrap,
  since this user tracks all configs in dotfiles).
- If it's a plugin skill, structure follows
  `plugin-name/skills/skill-name/{SKILL.md,references/,examples/,scripts/}`.

## Report format

```
## <skill-name>

- [severity] <finding> — <why it matters> — fix: <concrete suggestion>
- ...

Verdict: <one line>
```

Use severity `blocker` (skill won't trigger correctly or is broken),
`should-fix` (works but violates a documented best practice), or `nit`
(cosmetic). Skip the report entirely and just say "no problems found" if the
skill is genuinely clean — don't manufacture nits to seem thorough.
